Before calling submit_result, STOP and explicitly verify each item below. If ANY item fails, run a corrective query FIRST and only then submit.

content.text: I will now write a query to identify the top three third-page visits that occur after two consecutive visits to the '/detail' page. I will use the `LEAD` window function to create sequences of three consecutive page visits within each user session. Then, I will filter these sequences to isolate those that begin with two '/detail' visits, count the occurrences of each subsequent third-page visit, and rank them to find the three most frequent ones. To ensure accuracy, I will normalize the path by treating '/detail' and '/detail/' as the same page.

args.sql: WITH page_views AS (SELECT session, CASE WHEN path = '/detail/' THEN '/detail' ELSE path END AS page_path, stamp FROM log.main.activity_log), ranked_page_views AS (SELECT session, page_path, LEAD(page_path, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp) AS next_path, LEAD(page_path, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp) AS third_path FROM page_views) SELECT third_path, COUNT(*) AS count FROM ranked_page_views WHERE page_path = '/detail' AND next_path = '/detail' GROUP BY third_path ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 3;

content.text: I will refine my previous query to exclude sessions that end after two consecutive '/detail' visits. This will ensure that the results only include actual third-page visits, providing a more accurate answer to the user's question. I will then present the top three most frequent third-page visits based on this filtered data.

args.sql: WITH page_views AS (SELECT session, CASE WHEN path = '/detail/' THEN '/detail' ELSE path END AS page_path, stamp FROM log.main.activity_log), ranked_page_views AS (SELECT session, page_path, LEAD(page_path, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp) AS next_path, LEAD(page_path, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY session ORDER BY stamp) AS third_path FROM page_views) SELECT third_path, COUNT(*) AS count FROM ranked_page_views WHERE page_path = '/detail' AND next_path = '/detail' AND third_path IS NOT NULL GROUP BY third_path ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 3;

args.result_description: The table shows the top three most frequent third-page visits immediately following two consecutive visits to the '/detail' page. The 'third_path' column indicates the page visited, and the 'count' column shows how many times this sequence was observed.
